title: C L2 tx still labels profile-limit rejections of 256-264B unmatched packets as corruption (BUFFER_TOO_SMALL passthrough)
description: Found by correctness review pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-jfzk (P3, pre-existing class partially narrowed but not eliminated). lichen_link_tx's compressed buffer is 256 bytes (lichen_link_tx.c:43) while the SCHC Rule255 fallback needs 1+pkt_len; lichen_l2.h:215 gives tx_ipv6_buf = LICHEN_L2_MTU(200)+40+OSCORE overhead = 264. So a legitimate, policy-clean, rule-UNMATCHED packet (unprofiled UDP ports, ICMPv6 NS/NA/RA - the profile only has echo/DIO/DAO/CoAP/MQTT-SN rules) with pkt_len in [256..264] returns SCHC_ERR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL, which jfzk deliberately kept as a passthrough (internal sizing anomaly) and which lichen_l2_tx.c:159 still labels CRASH_STATE_CORRUPTION and maps raw -ENOENT to the net stack. Narrow window (only 9 byte-lengths, only unmatched rules), pre-existing, fail-closed either way. Fix direction: either size the compressed buffer to cover the fallback (e.g. min(1+ipv6_len, SCHC_FRAGMENT_MAX_PACKET_SIZE) on the stack - 265 bytes is affordable) so the fallback succeeds and the frame goes out uncompressed, or keep the cap and classify BUFFER_TOO_SMALL from the compress step as an operational rejection (skip crash_info, map -EINVAL) like LICHEN_ESCHC. Decide which behavior the profile wants (uncompressed delivery of unmatched-but-valid packets is what the Rust side does - rust compress falls back with usize::MAX single-frame limit and the caller buffer bounds), then align C and pin.
